sentences.text:
The insurer as well as the claimants are in appeal for the death of M. Lingaraju, a 53 years old,
who was working as a Secretary at Grama Panchayath.

The Tribunal has thereafter proceeded to award the following sums as compensation:
Towards loss of Financial Rs. 26,70,877/- Dependency Towards loss of Love and Rs.
20,000/-
 Affection  Towards loss of Rs. 40,000/-
 consortium  Towards loss of Estate Rs. 15,000/-
 Towards Funeral Rs. 15,000/-
 Expenses  Towards medical Rs. 1,66,000/-
 expenses
TOTAL Rs

2. The insurer has filed MFA No.3223/2018 contending that the accident occurred solely due to the negligence of the rider of the motor cycle and therefore, the fastening of the liability on the owner and the insurer was improper.
It is also contended that the compensation awarded is excessive.

3. The claimants on the other hand, contended that the finding recorded by the Tribunal that the driver of the offending vehicle, which had been insured by the appellant, was responsible for the accident.

It is also contended that though the deceased was hospitalized for 13 days, no sums have been awarded towards food,
nutrition, attendant and conveyance charges and the sums awarded towards loss of love and affection and the conventional heads are improper.
4. In order to establish that the deceased was himself responsible for the accident, the best witness would have been the driver of the offending vehicle, i.e., tempo traveller.
However, for reasons best known to the insurer, neither the driver was summoned nor were efforts made to examine him.
In the absence of any evidence to substantiate the allegation that the deceased was responsible for the accident, the insurer could not have been entitled to challenge the said finding.
It is also pertinent to state here that the driver of the insured vehicle had been charge sheeted and this also indicates that the negligence was on the part of the tempo traveller.
In my view, therefore, there is no merit in the appeal of the insurer insofar as it relates to the finding of negligence.

sentences.text: As far as the compensation is concerned, the tribunal has correctly taken the annual income of the deceased at Rs.3,23,742/- and has applied the proper multiplier.

6. Learned counsel for the insurer contends that the determination of the income at Rs.23,590/- is incorrect since Ex.P.10 indicated the amount of Rs.18,000/- was being remitted to the account of the deceased.

7. It is to be stated here that the deceased was working as a Secretary of Grama Panchayath and a certificate was issued by the Competent Authority indicating the salary that the deceased was getting.
8. Having regard to the fact that the claimant was working as a Secretary, it would be appropriate to accept the salary certificate that they have produced.

Merely because a lesser amount was remitted,
which could be due to various reasons, it cannot be assumed that the salary of the deceased was Rs.18,000/- This argument is therefore rejected.

9. The Tribunal, as stated above, has assessed the income correctly, applied the correct multiplier and also awarded proper future prospects and the amount awarded towards loss of dependency cannot be found fault with.

10. The claimants being the wife, children and parents, they would each be entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- towards "loss of consortium" i.e., in all Rs.1,76,000/- and they would also be entitled to a sum of Rs.33,000/- under the "conventional heads".
11. Evidence on record indicates that the deceased was hospitalized for 13 days and spent Rs.1,65,906/- for his treatment.
The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.1,66,000/- and the same would be just and proper.
12. However, it is noticed that no sums have been awarded towards food, nutrition, conveyance and attendant charges.

In my view, it is appropriate to award a sum of Rs.25,000/- towards food,
nutrition, conveyance and attendant charges.

13. Thus, the claimants, in modification of the impugned award, would be entitled to the following sums:
 Sl. Amount  Particulars  No.
(In Rs.)
1. Loss of Dependency 26,70,877  2. Loss of Consortium 1,76,000
3 . Conventional Heads 33,000

4. Medical expenses 1,66,000 Smt Vasantha vs Reliance General Insurance Company ... on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124127969/
5  5. Towards food, nutrition, 25,000  conveyance and attendant

14. Thus, the claimant would be entitled for compensation of Rs.30,70,877/- as against Rs.29,26,877/- awarded by the Tribunal, along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
15. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
16. The deposit and release of the compensation amount awarded shall be made as per the ratio adopted by the Tribunal.
17. The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transferred to the Tribunal for disbursal in terms of the award.
18. MFA No.5071/2018 filed by the claimants is accordingly allowed in part and MFA No.3223/2018 filed by the insurance company is dismissed.
